text: I built a door with no wall. People still knocked. I opened it and felt a strange new need to charge for the room.
My door says pull on both sides. I think it wants a fight. I have asked the wall to stay out of it.
I gave the door a day off. The room felt much larger. Then I found out how many people had been waiting to leave.
The door would not open for my best idea. I made the idea smaller. It got through and stopped acting so grand.
I put a sign on an open door. It said free. People asked what the catch was, so I added a fee to make them feel safe.
Someone sold me a door to the future. It led to a shop that sold doors. The future seems to have a strong view on repeat sales.
I asked the door to choose who could enter. It let in the wind. At least one guest came with no plan to fix me.
My door has a small glass hole. I can see trouble before I open it. This is called a feature, though it has not taught me to keep the door shut.
I moved the door to the other wall. The same room now feels like a fresh start. I hope change is always this cheap.
The door creaks when I tell a lie. I oil it once a week. The truth has become much harder to hear around here.
I made a map of places I had never seen. It sold well. People liked the lack of awkward details, such as where the road actually stopped.
My map says you are here. I moved it across the room. It still said the same thing. I admire a claim with such a strong defense.
I asked the map which path was best. It showed all the paths. I may have blamed it for work I never wanted to do myself.
The map had a blank patch. I called it a risk. My friend called it space to draw a park. We are still looking for the real ground beneath both views.
I drew a short path through a hill. The hill had some concerns. I have learned to ask the world before saving time on paper.
My map led to the sea. I had asked for a fresh start. Next time I will state that I plan to keep my feet dry.
I found a map inside a map. Both said to keep going. I have begun to suspect the maps are paid by the mile.
The map was upside down. I still got lost in the same place. This suggests a problem that cannot be fixed by a new view of the page.
I marked my goal with a star. The star was easy to reach with my pen. My legs have asked for a separate plan.
I keep a map of my mistakes. The page is getting dark. Soon I will be able to claim that I know the whole area.
I stood in a line to learn patience. It moved too fast. I now have a ticket and no clear proof that I have grown as a person.
My place in the line was marked with chalk. Rain moved me ahead three spots. I declined to call this hard work, though the chance was tempting.
I made a line for people who hate waiting. It is now the longest line in the room. I have built a fine home for a shared belief.
The person ahead of me let someone in. I felt the roots of a great speech begin to grow. Then they let me in too, and I lost my point.
I kept my place in line while my idea went for a walk. It came back with coffee. One of us is clearly ready for a larger role.
I joined the short line without reading the sign. It was for complaints. By the time I reached the front, I had developed a very good one.
The line stopped, so I walked to the front to learn why. A lost child was being helped. I folded my speech into a small and useful paper hat.
I drew a line between work and life. My work sent a note across it. I am now testing a wall, with a gate that shuts at six.
My line had a start and no end. People called it a journey. I called the person who sold me the ticket and asked about lunch.
I left the line for a moment and lost my place. It seems a great deal of status is just proof that someone has stood still for a long time.
